subject: photography
intro: Photography training leads to paid image-making and the careers around it — commissioned shoots, broadcast and film cameras, the edit suite, and the creative direction that commissions it all.

roles.title: Photographers
roles.what: Photograph people, landscapes, merchandise and other subjects, using lighting equipment to enhance a subject's appearance and editing software to produce finished images and prints, in commercial, industrial, scientific and news settings.
roles.where: The exposure triangle, metering and lighting topics from the camera unit, composition from the visual language unit, and RAW processing and printing from the digital workflow unit are the craft this work is hired for.

roles.title: Camera Operators, Television, Video, and Film
roles.what: Operate television, video or film cameras to record images and scenes for productions, working from shot plans and reacting live to unfolding action on set.
roles.where: Depth of field and motion control from the exposure unit, the decisive moment and framing from composition, and the documentary and modernist history unit give operators the visual instincts directors rely on.

roles.title: Film and Video Editors
roles.what: Edit moving images on film, video or other media, organising images with producers and directors into a final production and synchronising soundtracks with the picture.
roles.where: The digital workflow unit's RAW processing and editing ethics and limits, plus the history unit's staged versus straight photography debate, are exactly the judgement editors apply when assembling sequences.

roles.title: Art Directors
roles.what: Formulate design concepts and presentation approaches for visual productions and media such as print, broadcasting, video and film, and direct the workers engaged in artwork or layout design.
roles.where: The genres unit's portraiture and staged photography, the personal investigation's project development and critical evaluation, and composition theory prepare the concept-and-craft vocabulary directors use to lead creative teams.

roles.title: Graphic Designers
roles.what: Design or create graphics to meet commercial or promotional needs, such as packaging, displays and logos, using a variety of mediums to achieve artistic or decorative effects.
roles.where: Light and colour from the composition unit, the editing and presentation side of the print unit, and the research and contextual reference habits of the personal investigation transfer directly to commissioned visual design work.
